blocks.text: Status: CANONICAL — RENDERER/DECODER GATE MAY BEGIN
Next authorized gate: deterministic renderer and inverse decoder

The semantic IR is the language’s authoritative proposition layer. It represents meaning independently of English word order, absolute pitch, MIDI, glyph layout, or audio. Every utterance is a finite connected directed acyclic graph with one root clause. Nodes represent clauses, canonical lexical occurrences, literals, variables, references, scope operators, coordination, time anchors, measurements, and state snapshots. Typed edges express centers, semantic roles, scope, coordination membership, time relations, conditions, transitions, coreference, and discourse grounding.
The following dimensions must never be collapsed:
• modality such as possible, necessary, permitted, or obligated;

Runtime [0] does not mean “not.” Runtime [1] does not mean present tense or truth. Runtime [2]/num does not mean future tense or possible modality. A root lexically ending in trit 2 retains its canonical invariant regardless of the runtime state applied to a particular occurrence.

The IR preserves the Core 1.0 actor/source/cause, predicate, target/result/destination, and background roles and adds typed roles needed for complete propositions, including experiencer, bearer, content, recipient, instrument, material, location, time, manner, quantity, comparison standard, and beneficiary. Roles are explicit; adjacency cannot supply a missing participant.

Negation, modality, quantification, aspect, and repetition are scope operators with one exact scope. References resolve through declared referent IDs and explicit coreference edges. An unresolved reference produces an error or clarification request rather than a guessed antecedent.

Quantifiers distinguish exact, at-least, at-most, range, all, some, none, and proportional readings. Measurements use canonical decimal magnitudes and controlled units. Quantifier “none” is not the same as negating a whole clause.

Tense is represented through explicit before, at, after, during, starts, ends, or overlaps relations to speech time, reference time, absolute time, or an interval. Transition clauses require one explicit before-state and one explicit after-state; a lexical process alone does not silently provide either snapshot.

Coordination distinguishes all-of, any-of, exactly-one, sequence, and parallel structure. Sequences require contiguous order beginning at one. Parallel members have no serial order. Repetition specifies a finite count, while-condition, or until-condition. Clause embedding and compound references may recurse only through a finite acyclic expanded graph.

Canonical execution validates schema, lexical authority, graph structure, cardinality, scope, bindings, quantities, time, transitions, and serialization in a fixed order. Semantic payloads serialize as canonical UTF-8 JSON and receive content-derived UTT identifiers from SHA-256 digests.

“Executable grammar” means the IR has deterministic validation, binding, scope, evaluation order, diagnostics, and serialization. It does not mean an English parser, renderer, inverse decoder, MIDI engine, glyph generator, or translator exists yet. The next release must map canonical IR to formal notation, family-qualified forms, carriers, notes, runtime endings, contours, timing, and registers, then decode that realization back to the identical IR under round-trip tests.
